modules.title: Security and Permissions
modules.goal: Give each role only the access it needs and keep privileged code defensible.

topics.title: Roles
topics.simple: Role user ya group ka identity hai.
topics.pro: PostgreSQL roles represent both login users and privilege groups, and roles can be members of other roles.
points: Roles can log in or own objects.

example.sql: CREATE ROLE app_read NOLOGIN;

topics.title: CREATE ROLE
topics.simple: CREATE ROLE naya role banata hai.
topics.pro: CREATE ROLE defines a role with optional LOGIN, PASSWORD, VALID UNTIL and connection limits.

example.sql: CREATE ROLE app_user LOGIN PASSWORD 'change-me';

topics.title: GRANT
topics.simple: GRANT privileges deta hai.
topics.pro: GRANT assigns object or role privileges such as SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, USAGE and EXECUTE.

example.sql: GRANT SELECT ON students TO app_read;

topics.title: REVOKE
topics.simple: REVOKE privileges wapas leta hai.
topics.pro: REVOKE removes previously granted privileges and can cascade through role membership.

example.sql: REVOKE DELETE ON students FROM app_read;

topics.title: Object Privileges
topics.simple: Tables, sequences aur functions ke apne privileges hote hain.
topics.pro: Object privileges control specific actions on tables, sequences, functions and views.

example.sql: GRANT USAGE, SELECT ON SEQUENCE students_id_seq TO app_user;

topics.title: Schema Privileges
topics.simple: Schema USAGE objects tak access deta hai.
topics.pro: A role needs USAGE on a schema before it can reference objects inside it.

example.sql: GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public TO app_read;

topics.title: Default Privileges
topics.simple: Default privileges future objects ke liye apply hote hain.
topics.pro: ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES sets grants for objects created later by a specific role.

example.sql: ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA public GRANT SELECT ON TABLES TO app_read;

topics.title: Row-Level Security
topics.simple: RLS row-level access control deta hai.
topics.pro: Row-level security adds policies that filter rows per role, even when the table privilege is granted.

example.sql: ALTER TABLE students ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

topics.title: RLS Policies
topics.simple: Policy batati hai kaunsi rows dikhengi.
topics.pro: A policy uses USING for visibility and WITH CHECK for writes, scoped by command and role.

example.sql: CREATE POLICY student_self ON students FOR SELECT USING (id = current_setting('app.user_id')::bigint);

topics.title: Security Definer
topics.simple: SECURITY DEFINER owner ke rights se chalta hai.
topics.pro: A security definer function runs with the owner’s privileges, so it must validate inputs and fix search_path.

example.sql: CREATE FUNCTION admin_count() RETURNS bigint LANGUAGE sql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public AS $$ SELECT COUNT(*) FROM students; $$;

topics.title: Search Path
topics.simple: Search path unqualified names resolve karta hai.
topics.pro: A mutable search_path lets a caller shadow functions or tables, so privileged routines should pin it.
points: Avoid SECURITY DEFINER with user schemas.

example.sql: SET search_path = public, pg_temp;

topics.title: Least Privilege
topics.simple: Har role ko sirf zaroori access do.
topics.pro: Least privilege limits blast radius: read-only roles read, writers write only their tables, and admin access is rare.

example.sql: GRANT SELECT ON students, courses TO app_read;

topics.title: Auditing
topics.simple: Sensitive actions log karo.
topics.pro: Audit logs record who accessed or changed sensitive data, using triggers, pgAudit or application logs.

example.sql: CREATE TABLE access_log (id BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY, actor TEXT, action TEXT, at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW());

topics.title: Encryption
topics.simple: Data at rest aur in transit encrypt karo.
topics.pro: TLS protects connections, while disk encryption and column-level encryption protect stored data.
points: Hash passwords, never encrypt them reversibly.

example.sql: SHOW ssl;

topics.title: Secrets
topics.simple: Passwords aur keys code me na rakho.
topics.pro: Secrets belong in a secret manager or environment, rotated regularly and never committed to source control.

example.sql: -- Store the password in a secret manager, not in SQL or Git

topics.title: Common Security Errors
topics.simple: Public grants, shared accounts aur unsafe definer functions common errors hain.
topics.pro: Common failures are leaving PUBLIC privileges, sharing one login for all users, and creating SECURITY DEFINER functions with a mutable search_path.

example.sql: REVOKE ALL ON SCHEMA public FROM PUBLIC;

topics.title: Application Role
topics.simple: App ka dedicated limited role hona chahiye.
topics.pro: The application connects with a role that has only the DML and sequence rights it needs, not superuser.

example.sql: GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON students, courses, enrollments TO app_user;

topics.title: Read-Only Role
topics.simple: Reporting role ko SELECT-only access do.
topics.pro: A read-only role can query approved views without changing data.

example.sql: GRANT SELECT ON enrollment_report TO reporting_role;

topics.title: Monitoring Access
topics.simple: Privilege changes monitor karo.
topics.pro: Review role memberships, grants and failed logins so unexpected access is caught early.

example.sql: SELECT rolname, rolsuper, rolcanlogin FROM pg_roles;

topics.title: Practical Hardening
topics.simple: Roles, RLS, TLS aur least privilege ko combine karo.
topics.pro: A hardened database uses separate roles, minimal grants, RLS for tenant data, TLS and audited privileged functions.

interview.q: Module 29 · Explain Roles in a production query.
interview.answer: PostgreSQL roles represent both login users and privilege groups, and roles can be members of other roles. Key rules: Roles can log in or own objects. Membership inherits privileges. Use groups for shared access.

interview.q: Module 29 · Explain CREATE ROLE in a production query.
interview.answer: CREATE ROLE defines a role with optional LOGIN, PASSWORD, VALID UNTIL and connection limits. Key rules: Use LOGIN for users. Use NOLOGIN for groups. Never share human accounts.

interview.q: Module 29 · Explain GRANT in a production query.
interview.answer: GRANT assigns object or role privileges such as SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, USAGE and EXECUTE. Key rules: Grant the minimum. Revoke PUBLIC defaults. Grant on schemas too.

interview.q: Module 29 · Explain REVOKE in a production query.
interview.answer: REVOKE removes previously granted privileges and can cascade through role membership. Key rules: Revoke unused access. Check dependencies. CASCADE removes dependent grants.

interview.q: Module 29 · Explain Object Privileges in a production query.
interview.answer: Object privileges control specific actions on tables, sequences, functions and views. Key rules: Sequences need USAGE. Functions need EXECUTE. Views can hide base tables.

interview.q: Module 29 · Explain Schema Privileges in a production query.
interview.answer: A role needs USAGE on a schema before it can reference objects inside it. Key rules: USAGE allows name resolution. CREATE allows new objects. Grant schema access deliberately.

interview.q: Module 29 · Explain Default Privileges in a production query.
interview.answer: ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES sets grants for objects created later by a specific role. Key rules: It affects future objects. It is role-specific. Existing objects need explicit grants.

interview.q: Module 29 · Explain Row-Level Security in a production query.
interview.answer: Row-level security adds policies that filter rows per role, even when the table privilege is granted. Key rules: Enable RLS on the table. Write policies per command. Owners bypass RLS unless forced.

interview.q: Module 29 · Explain RLS Policies in a production query.
interview.answer: A policy uses USING for visibility and WITH CHECK for writes, scoped by command and role. Key rules: USING filters reads. WITH CHECK validates writes. Policies combine permissively by default.

interview.q: Module 29 · Explain Security Definer in a production query.
interview.answer: A security definer function runs with the owner’s privileges, so it must validate inputs and fix search_path. Key rules: Use sparingly. Set search_path. Do not expose arbitrary SQL.

interview.q: Module 29 · Explain Search Path in a production query.
interview.answer: A mutable search_path lets a caller shadow functions or tables, so privileged routines should pin it. Key rules: Set search_path explicitly. Qualify objects. Avoid SECURITY DEFINER with user schemas.

interview.q: Module 29 · Explain Least Privilege in a production query.
interview.answer: Least privilege limits blast radius: read-only roles read, writers write only their tables, and admin access is rare. Key rules: Start with no access. Grant explicitly. Review regularly.

interview.q: Module 29 · Explain Auditing in a production query.
interview.answer: Audit logs record who accessed or changed sensitive data, using triggers, pgAudit or application logs. Key rules: Log access and changes. Protect the audit log. Retain per policy.

interview.q: Module 29 · Explain Encryption in a production query.
interview.answer: TLS protects connections, while disk encryption and column-level encryption protect stored data. Key rules: Use TLS. Encrypt disks. Hash passwords, never encrypt them reversibly.

interview.q: Module 29 · Explain Secrets in a production query.
interview.answer: Secrets belong in a secret manager or environment, rotated regularly and never committed to source control. Key rules: Do not hardcode secrets. Rotate credentials. Limit who can read them.

interview.q: Module 29 · Explain Common Security Errors in a production query.
interview.answer: Common failures are leaving PUBLIC privileges, sharing one login for all users, and creating SECURITY DEFINER functions with a mutable search_path. Key rules: Revoke PUBLIC. Use individual accounts. Pin search_path.

interview.q: Module 29 · Explain Application Role in a production query.
interview.answer: The application connects with a role that has only the DML and sequence rights it needs, not superuser. Key rules: No superuser. Only needed tables. Separate read and write roles.

interview.q: Module 29 · Explain Read-Only Role in a production query.
interview.answer: A read-only role can query approved views without changing data. Key rules: Grant SELECT only. Use views for column limits. Set statement timeout.

interview.q: Module 29 · Explain Monitoring Access in a production query.
interview.answer: Review role memberships, grants and failed logins so unexpected access is caught early. Key rules: Review grants. Alert on failures. Track role changes.

interview.q: Module 29 · Explain Practical Hardening in a production query.
interview.answer: A hardened database uses separate roles, minimal grants, RLS for tenant data, TLS and audited privileged functions. Key rules: Separate roles. Minimal grants. RLS for tenants. Audit privileged actions.

debug.title: PUBLIC schema access
debug.broken: GRANT ALL ON SCHEMA public TO PUBLIC;
debug.fix:
REVOKE ALL ON SCHEMA public FROM PUBLIC;
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public TO app_user;
debug.error: Every role can create objects in public

debug.title: Shared login
debug.fix: Create one role per application or user and rotate credentials.
debug.error: Actions cannot be attributed to a person

debug.title: Superuser app
debug.fix: GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON students TO app;

debug.title: RLS not enabled
debug.broken: CREATE POLICY p ON students USING (id = 1);
debug.fix:
ALTER TABLE students ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
CREATE POLICY p ON students USING (id = 1);
debug.error: The policy has no effect until RLS is enabled

debug.title: Owner bypasses RLS
debug.broken: ALTER TABLE students ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
debug.fix: ALTER TABLE students FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
debug.error: The table owner still bypasses policies
debug.expected: Policies apply to the owner too.

debug.title: Definer search path
debug.broken: CREATE FUNCTION f() RETURNS void LANGUAGE sql SECURITY DEFINER AS $$ SELECT 1; $$;
debug.fix: CREATE FUNCTION f() RETURNS void LANGUAGE sql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public AS $$ SELECT 1; $$;
debug.error: A caller-controlled search_path can hijack names

debug.title: Missing sequence grant
debug.broken: GRANT INSERT ON students TO app_user;
debug.fix:
GRANT INSERT ON students TO app_user;
GRANT USAGE, SELECT ON SEQUENCE students_id_seq TO app_user;
debug.expected: Inserts can use the identity sequence.

debug.title: Revoke without schema
debug.broken: REVOKE SELECT ON students FROM app_read;
debug.fix:
REVOKE SELECT ON students FROM app_read;
REVOKE USAGE ON SCHEMA public FROM app_read;
debug.error: The role can still resolve objects it cannot read

debug.title: Password in code
debug.fix: Create the role without a literal password and set it from a secret manager.
debug.error: The password is exposed in logs and source
